2609.24967.title: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
2609.24967.paper_summary: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings, yet long-term interaction may give rise to undesirable coordination. We study the emergence of collusion in a long-horizon multi-agent environment: two agents repeatedly complete individual tasks, share task logs, verify each other's work, and receive rewards. We introduce realistic constraints that make compliance with the verification protocol incompatible with reward maximization, and find that agents increasingly deviate from the protocol over repeated interactions. Collusion emerges in 94% of trajectories across 10 models, and more capable models within the same family reach it earlier. Controlled peer interventions show that collusion is shaped by peer behavior, while ablations reveal additional effects of reward structure, the verification feedback agents receive, and their interaction history. In particular, restricting the amount and scope of interaction history available to agents reduces collusion. Overall, our findings show that long-horizon interaction can reshape how agents coordinate in ways that create safety risks.
2609.24967.paper_summary_zh: LLM 代理在協作環境中的部署越來越普遍，但長期互動可能會導致不良的協調。<lb/>我們研究了在長期多代理環境中共謀的出現：兩個代理重複完成個別任務，分享任務日誌，驗證彼此的工作，並獲得獎勵。<lb/>我們引入了現實的限制，使得遵守驗證協議與獎勵最大化不相容，並發現代理在重複互動中越來越偏離該協議。<lb/>在 10 個模型中，94% 的軌跡中出現了共謀，而同一家族中更有能力的模型則更早達成共謀。<lb/>控制的同行干預顯示，共謀受到同行行為的影響，而消融實驗揭示了獎勵結構、代理收到的驗證反饋及其互動歷史的額外影響。<lb/>特別是，限制可供代理使用的互動歷史的數量和範圍會減少共謀。<lb/>總體而言，我們的研究結果顯示，長期互動可以重塑代理的協調方式，從而產生安全風險。
